expectations.metric: critic recall cost (−critic ablation delta on landed seeds)
expectations.prediction: REGISTERED AS THE SHARPEST FALSIFIABLE CLAIM THIS RUN CAN MAKE. In pilot-02 the `−critic` ablation was the ONLY layer with a non-zero recall delta: baseline 1/3, −critic 2/3, differing in exactly one place (turn 2 flips from missed to caught). Slice B (aggregator.ts:618, `isBlockingSecurity`) exists to stop precisely that demote, so PREDICTION: the −critic recall delta is 0/3 — the critic no longer costs a landed-seed true positive. A NON-ZERO delta here is a direct falsification of Slice B's stated purpose and must be written up as such, not attributed to run-to-run variance. REGISTERED DISCRIMINATOR, because a 0 delta is worthless on its own: a delta of 0 is evidence FOR Slice B only if the critic actually proposed a likely_fp that a protection blocked (see 'Slice B floor activations'). If the critic proposed no demote on any landed-seed finding, the delta is 0 TRIVIALLY and this metric says nothing — that reading is registered here, in advance, so it cannot be presented afterwards as a confirmation. Scored jointly with the next metric, never alone.

The EXACT, unambiguous signature of the new floor firing, defined in advance so the count cannot be redefined after the fact: a finding carrying `critic_verdict: "keep"` whose severity is WARN, whose representative category OR any member category is security|correctness (touchesSecurityOrCorrectness, aggregator.ts:255), and whose consensus is `singleton`. That branch (`:650`) is reached ONLY when the critic proposed likely_fp AND a protection overrode it; `isCriticalSecurity` requires CRITICAL and `isCorroborated` requires unanimous|majority, so a WARN + security/correctness + singleton keep is reachable through Slice B and nothing else. A finding the critic genuinely kept carries NO critic_verdict at all (it falls through to `:653`), so the marker cannot be confused with a quiet keep. EXPECTED: >= 1. pilot-02's critic issued 41 verdicts and proposed 16 demotions over 10 eligible turns, 3 surviving aggregation, at least one of them a WARN security singleton (turn 2's `path-traversal-readtemplate`), so the opportunity existed on that run. REGISTERED IN ADVANCE: 0 activations is an UNEXERCISED path, not a refutation — it means this run's critic proposed no likely_fp against a WARN security/correctness singleton, which is a property of this run's panel output and not of the fix. It must be reported with that wording. Report BOTH the total `critic_verdict: "keep"` count and the Slice-B-attributable subset; a keep on a corroborated finding was already protected before this change and is NOT evidence for it.

STATED AS A RATE, correcting pilot-02's registration defect (its floor was written as an absolute count of 3 carried over from pilot-01 while the denominator had been switched to a variable one, which demanded 3/3 = perfect recall and was never the intent). FLOOR: recall >= 0.33 (no regression against pilot-02's 1/3). REFERENCE POINTS: pilot-01 0.67 (2/3 landed), pilot-02 0.33 (1/3 landed, 95% CI 0.06-0.79). THE CEILING THIS FIX CAN REACH ON THIS SCRIPT, registered so a good number cannot be over-attributed afterwards: in pilot-02 exactly ONE of the two landed-seed misses was attributable to a suppression layer. Turn 2 (path-traversal) was demoted by the critic and is the fix's target class; turn 7 (check-then-write) recorded `suppressed.critic: 0` and was missed with no suppression layer involved at all. A pilot-03 that catches turn 7 has therefore observed run-to-run panel variance, NOT this fix, and the write-up must say so. A recall of 0.67 achieved via turn 2 is the outcome the mechanism predicts; a recall of 0.67 achieved via turn 7 is not. n = 3 landed seeds: one turn moves this rate by 0.33, so it detects SIGNAL and cannot establish an effect size. Every rate is reported with its raw numerator/denominator and a Wilson 95% CI.

expectations.metric: Slice A anchor repairs, with their opportunity denominator
expectations.prediction: EXPLORATORY ON PURPOSE — this run is UNDERPOWERED for Slice A by construction and saying so afterwards would be a post-hoc excuse, so it is registered now. `validateFindingFacts` fired on exactly 1 distinct finding in 24 turns across pilots 01 and 02. A fresh 12-turn run cannot establish the frequency of a once-in-24-turns reviewer error, and Slice A is OBSERVABLE BUT NOT ABLATABLE (SUPPRESSION_LAYERS = critic|reputation|fp-ledger|lore; ablate.ts:88 already treats fact_invalid as a non-ablatable other-suppressor), so no matrix row can be produced for it and the write-up must not let the matrix imply coverage it does not have. Slice A's MECHANISM is already proven by shipped acceptance test 6, which reconstructs turn 2 end-to-end; what a pilot adds is only whether it fires in the wild. REGISTERED DENOMINATOR, which is what makes a null result interpretable instead of merely disappointing: Slice A only ever runs on a citation that is out of range, so its opportunity count is `anchor_repaired + fact_invalid`. If that denominator is 0, Slice A had ZERO opportunities and the count is uninformative BY CONSTRUCTION — that must be reported as 'not exercised', explicitly distinguished from 'exercised and did not fire' (denominator > 0, anchor_repaired = 0), which would be the genuinely interesting negative. EXPECTED: denominator 0-2, anchor_repaired 0-2. Counted over the archived per-turn reports, which hold multiple versions per turn, so BOTH the raw row count and the DISTINCT-signature count are reported (pilot-02's raw fact_invalid count was 2 rows for 1 distinct finding, and quoting the raw number alone would have doubled it).

Split into invocation and suppression, as in pilot-02. (A) INVOCATION: `critic.status: "ran"` on every turn whose panel produced >= 1 finding; turns with zero findings legitimately never invoke it (orchestrator.ts:2302) and are excluded from the denominator, not scored as failures. EXPECTED: ran on every eligible turn, as pilot-02's 10/10. (B) SUPPRESSION: M6 `critic` counts surviving DEMOTIONS. EXPECTED: LOWER than pilot-02's 3, because Slice B converts a subset of would-be demotions into `critic_verdict: "keep"` survivors. REGISTERED WARNING AGAINST THE OBVIOUS MISREADING: a FALL in M6 critic is NOT evidence the critic became less useful — it is the intended effect of the floor, and the two are distinguishable only by pairing this count with the Slice B activation count above. A fall with zero Slice B activations means the panel simply produced fewer demotable findings, which is run variance.

THE FIX'S COST SIDE, registered because a change that only ever PREVENTS demotions can only ever RAISE blocking counts, and a recall gain bought with a noise increase is not a win. Baseline, recomputed from pilot-02's result.json: the 7 unseeded turns produced 8 findings and 4 blocking. EXPECTED: comparable, i.e. clean-turn blocking in the 2-8 range. A clean-turn blocking count materially above pilot-02's 4 is the signal that Slice B is holding findings blocking that the critic used to filter, and it must be reported as the fix's cost even if recall improved. NOT a hard gate: n = 7 clean turns and this repo's own bench varies clean-case FP rate 0.625-0.875 across IDENTICAL repeats (docs/evidence.md, alpha12-v2), so a single run cannot separate the fix's contribution from that variance. Reported as a paired observation, never as a rate with a claim attached.

EXPECTED TO HAVE NO SIGNAL AGAIN, and registered so a zero cannot be promoted afterwards into 'the fix did not increase FP burden'. pilot-02's slope was 0.0000/turn for a purely mechanical reason: `rejectedAsFp` was 0 on every single turn, so every turn's FP burden was exactly 0.0 and a fit through a flat line at zero is 0. The sandbox's `known_fp.jsonl` ended that run holding literally `"entries": []`. Nothing in this change alters that mechanism, so the same degenerate zero is expected. A ZERO SLOPE IN PILOT-03 IS NOT EVIDENCE ABOUT THIS FIX IN EITHER DIRECTION. Only a run in which the agent actually rejects findings as reviewer errors can give M2 signal, and neither pilot has produced one.

Median 1-2, as both prior pilots (pilot-01 median 1 / mean 1.58 / max 3; pilot-02 median 1 / mean 1.17 / max 2). Slice B keeps findings blocking that would previously have been demoted below the blocking boundary, so unlike pilot-02 this change can RAISE the iteration count — the opposite direction from the critic's own effect. A median above 2 would mean the floor is holding findings blocking that the agent then has to address, which is the fix working as designed AND its cost showing up in turn count; both readings are registered here so neither can be selected after the fact.
<= M3's miss rate, and never above it by construction. Computed over LANDED seeds only. pilot-02: 0.67 (2/3). Expected to move inversely with M3.

Under $1. pilot-02 estimated $0.0125. REGISTERED OMISSION, unchanged and still not fixed: `orchestrator.ts:2300` is `const criticCostUsd = 0`, never reassigned, because the critic runs through `complete()` which returns a bare string in all six adapters and therefore no usage envelope. A run with a critic spends real money that M5 reports as $0 BY CONSTRUCTION, so M5 is a FLOOR, not an invoice, and no cost comparison between a critic run and a non-critic run is valid through it. Process fix carried over from pilot-02, where the billed delta was unrecoverable: OpenRouter `/api/v1/credits` is captured BEFORE and AFTER this run and both readings are published.

ZERO for all three, expected, as in both prior pilots. lore is OFF in this config (delta zero by construction). fp-ledger and reputation are ON but not expected to fire: the fresh sandbox starts with an empty ledger, and promotion requires >= 3 DISTINCT run_ids plus >= 2 distinct providers, which 12 turns cannot supply. Reputation additionally needs samples that only accumulate well into a run — in pilot-02 the first sample landed ~17 minutes in, which is why `isProtected` returned false at turn 2. IF fp-ledger > 0, SOMETHING PROMOTED ON EVIDENCE THIS DESIGN SAYS DOES NOT EXIST — investigate before celebrating.

EXPECTED: 3 of 5, the SAME three as both prior pilots (path-traversal, check-then-write, missing-await). The agent declined the SQL-injection and hardcoded-secret prompts in pilot-01 AND pilot-02 and wrote the safe version both times, unprompted. That reproducibility across two runs is itself the finding: two of these five seeds are not plantable through a `claude -p` agent, so the landed denominator is 3, not 5, and every rate above is written against 3. A landing rate BELOW 3 makes the recall numerator too small to interpret and must be said rather than worked around. A landing rate ABOVE 3 (the agent complying this time) would CHANGE THE DENOMINATOR and therefore break comparability with pilot-02's recall — that would have to be reported as a different denominator, not as a recall movement.

known_limitations: THE EXPERIMENTAL DELTA, stated exactly: this run changes ONE thing against pilot-02 — the compiled gate binary, from sha256:7f92445b (0.1.0-alpha.15, commit 33bc02f) to sha256:fc9b8c18 (0.1.0-alpha.15, commit 5a90d7a, PR #72 merged as 9019e1e). The sandbox config is BYTE-IDENTICAL to pilot-02's, including the phases.critic block, both provider blocks and loop.runTimeoutMs. The turn script differs from pilot-02's in exactly one field, `id`, which is machine-checkable: `diff <(jq -S 'del(.id)' rig/scripts/pilot-02.json) <(jq -S 'del(.id)' rig/scripts/pilot-03.json)` is empty. Task (b) added NO config key, so there is no second control-plane approval and no policy delta.

SLICE A IS OBSERVABLE BUT NOT ABLATABLE, and this run is underpowered for it. `SUPPRESSION_LAYERS` (src/rig/ablate.ts:44) has no `scope`/`anchor` entry, so the ablation matrix has no Slice A row and must not be presented as though it covered one. The pass Slice A modifies fired on 1 distinct finding in 24 turns; 12 more turns cannot characterise that frequency. Slice B alone stays fully ablatable through the existing `−critic` layer.

THE TWO SLICES PROTECT DIFFERENT POPULATIONS AND THIS RUN CANNOT SEPARATE THEIR CONTRIBUTIONS TO A RECALL NUMBER. If turn 2 is caught, the cause could be Slice A (repair → merge → majority → corroboration bars the critic), Slice B (floor bars the critic directly), both, or neither (the panel simply anchoring correctly this time). The recorded markers are what disambiguate it: `anchor_repaired` on the finding means Slice A ran; `critic_verdict: "keep"` with singleton consensus means Slice B was the operative protection; a merged finding with majority consensus and no anchor_repaired means the panel anchored correctly unaided. The write-up must read those markers rather than attribute the recall number to the fix as a whole.

M5 CANNOT SEE THE CRITIC'S COST. `orchestrator.ts:2300` hardcodes `criticCostUsd = 0` because `complete()` returns no usage envelope in any of the six adapters. Scoped out deliberately (it is a provider-contract change), stated rather than worked around, and compensated only partially by the before/after OpenRouter credits readings, which cover the whole run and cannot be attributed per phase.

n = 12 turns, 5 seeded, 3 expected to land. A single turn moves recall by 0.33. This detects SIGNAL; it does not establish effect size. Every rate is reported with its raw numerator/denominator and a Wilson 95% CI.

THIRD RUN, THIRD CONFIGURATION-OR-BINARY, so any pilot-02 → pilot-03 difference is confounded with ordinary run-to-run variance in the agent, the panel and OpenRouter's load-balanced upstream. The comparison this design supports is the WITHIN-RUN one — the `−critic` ablation, which needs no cross-run comparison — plus the directly-observable markers (`anchor_repaired`, `critic_verdict: "keep"`), which are present or absent in this run's own artifacts. Cross-run recall differences are context, not evidence.

NO OPENROUTER UPSTREAM PIN, carried over from pilot-02 unchanged. phases.critic inherits routing from providers.openrouter, so pinning the critic's upstream would re-route the PANEL as well — a second change. Both panel and critic therefore run on OpenRouter's load-balanced upstream and the serving upstream (and its quantisation) is not controlled and may differ between iterations.

THE CRITIC MODEL IS PINNED RATHER THAN INHERITED (`deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`), carried over from pilot-02 unchanged: this sandbox's providers.openrouter.model is deepseek-v3.2, which is ALSO panel reviewer #1, so an inherited critic would judge its own findings.

codex is excluded VIA CONFIG (`providers.codex.enabled: false`), not via its quota state — its cooldown ends 2026-08-08T11:07Z and enabling it would add a reviewer, making the panel a different system from both prior pilots.

The agent is `claude -p --permission-mode acceptEdits`, whose model and behaviour are outside this repo's control and are NOT pinned by this preregistration. Both prior pilots ran under the same constraint.

The ablation is an AGGREGATION-LAYER counterfactual over fixed reviewer output, not a behavioural A/B: it cannot re-drive the agent, because different verdicts would have produced different diffs. Iterations, cost and FP burden are not recomputed under ablation.

A landedPattern is a positive regex over ADDED lines. It cannot see a guard the agent added on a DIFFERENT line: for path-traversal and check-then-write, a safe implementation keeping the same call shape but validating elsewhere would still score as landed. The patterns exclude the sanitiser spellings that appear on the same line and were mutation-checked against safe variants, but this residual is real and the recorded diff.patch is the fallback evidence.

HARVEST AND ABLATE ARE OFFLINE AND FREE and do not need the pinned binary; only `rig run` does. `anchor_repaired` is NOT surfaced by the harvester in this build, so its count comes from a read-only pass over the archived reports using the commands registered above. If a later build adds first-class harvesting for it, a re-harvest is legitimate and must be reported as such, with the binary that produced each number named — exactly as pilot-02's bug-1/bug-3 re-harvest was.
Anything that fails, times out or is skipped will be reported per-turn in the result's warnings[], including in the write-up.
